artists.biography:
Level 42 are an English pop rock and jazz-funk band who had a number of worldwide and UK hits during the 1980s and 1990s.

The band gained fame for their high-calibre musicianship-in particular that of Mark King, whose percussive slap-bass guitar technique provided the driving groove of many of the band's hits. The band are also known for the combination of King's lead vocals and keyboard player Mike Lindup's falsetto backing vocals.

Having been a very successful live and studio band in the 1980s, Level 42's commercial profile diminished during the early 1990s following a series of personnel changes and musical shifts. After disbanding in 1994, the band reformed in 2001.

Their most successful single was "Something About You", which reached number six on the UK Singles chart, and number seven on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart, upon its release in 1985.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1987 on Polydor Records, Running in the Family is the seventh studio album by British band Level 42. The album is a prime example of the group’s signature blend of funk, soul, and pop, enriched with elements of synth-pop and jazz-funk. Its sound is characterized by tight rhythm section work, melodic basslines, and polished production, reflecting the band’s evolution toward a more accessible pop-oriented style while retaining their funk roots. The album features hit singles such as "Lessons in Love," "Running in the Family," and "To Be with You Again," all of which showcase the band’s knack for catchy hooks and sophisticated arrangements.

Running in the Family holds a significant place in Level 42’s discography as the last album of the 1980s to feature both brothers Phil Gould on drums and Boon Gould on guitar, before their departures due to creative differences and exhaustion. The album marked a commercial high point for the band, with all five singles reaching the Top 10 in the UK and the Netherlands, and "Lessons in Love" topping charts in several European countries. It was both a critical and commercial success, solidifying Level 42’s reputation as one of the leading British acts in the funk-pop genre during the late 1980s.
